lines.say: This week, Italy said two of its citizens were killed in an Iranian strike in Kuwait.
But in 1990, Kuwait was invaded, and the whole Gulf was pulled into war.
On August 2nd, 1990, Iraq's army invaded Kuwait, and took it in two days.
President George H. W. Bush declared the invasion would not stand.
American troops poured into Saudi Arabia to defend the kingdom and its oil.
When coalition air strikes began, Iraq fired Scud missiles, and Patriot batteries shot back.
Six weeks later, Kuwait was free. Retreating troops left its oil wells burning for months.
Now Kuwait is under fire again, and the Gulf is on edge.
Could today's Gulf crisis become another Gulf War?
